title: Patient Terms for Appeals of Prior Authorization Denials — Prescription Insurance on File
content:
These terms apply to appeals of prior authorization denials on a plan held under **Prescription Insurance on File**.

**1. Who files.** An appeal is the patient's own request to the plan and is filed only by the patient, never by Kestrel on the patient's behalf.

**2. Filing deadline.** An appeal of a denial is filed no later than the date the plan denied the prior authorization plus the class's appeal filing window days, counted in calendar days with the denial date as day 0. The denial date is the date the denial carries on the coverage's prior authorization record, and an appeal filed on the last day of the window is in time.

**3. One appeal per denial.** One appeal is filed per denial; a denial that already has an appeal filed against it takes no second appeal.

**4. Decision due date.** The former clause — that the decision due date is the filing date plus the class's standard appeal decision days, or, when the prescriber attests urgency, the filing moment plus the class's expedited appeal decision hours rounded up to the calendar date on which the last hour falls — is **no longer in force**. It has been superseded by the current basis, under which an appeal is recorded with its own appeal decision window.

**5. Outcome.** An overturned appeal is recorded with its approval end date, and claims then follow the approval rules for prior authorizations. An upheld denial is final at the Patient Care Desk, and any further review is between the patient and the plan.

## Filing deadline boundary (hypothetical: denial on 1 March, 60-day window)

| Appeal filed on | Day count from the denial | In time? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 March | day 0 | Yes |
| 30 April | day 60 | Yes — last day |
| 1 May | day 61 | No |

## Questions these terms answer

- *May Kestrel file the appeal for the patient?* No; the appeal is filed only by the patient.
- *May a second appeal be filed against the same denial?* No; one appeal is filed per denial.
- *What happens after an upheld denial?* It is final at the Patient Care Desk; any further review is between the patient and the plan.

superseded_clauses: Its decision_due_date is the filing date plus appeal_decision_standard_days, or, when the prescriber attests urgency, the filing moment plus appeal_decision_expedited_hours rounded up to the calendar date on which the last hour falls.
